newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke dips after Hilton move for ITT.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke dips after Hilton move for ITT.

text.p: Shares in British hotel and betting company Ladbroke Group Plc dipped 3.5p to 225p on Tuesday in heavy trade after partner Hilton Hotels Corp made a $10.5 billion bid for ITT Corp.
Analysts said the Hilton move was likely to mean its newly sealed worldwide alliance with Ladbroke would assume a lower priority.
Ladbroke and Hilton Hotels Corp (HHC) signed an agreement on January 13 to reunite the Hilton hotel brand worldwide for the first time since 1964.
HHC owns the rights to the Hilton name in the U.S. while Ladbroke holds them elsewhere in the world.
The alliance allows for each company to take a stake of up to 20 percent in the other and HHC has said it intends to acquire a five percent stake in Ladbroke in due course.
Analyst Greg Feehely at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson said HHC was likely to take a five percent stake after Ladbrokes' results in March but may now take longer to raise this to 20 percent.
Feehely said that Dresdner Kleinwort Benson still regarded Ladbroke as a "buy".
"We are not going to see the stock coming off much. It is still solidly underpinned and there may be potential for Ladbroke to invest in ITT's non-U.S. assets," he said.
"At the turn of the decade all this might just be one company," added Feehely.
A Ladbroke spokesman said that the HHC move should not affect the alliance. He noted that HHC would have been planning the ITT bid when it signed up to the alliance.
"Having done the deal for Bally and the alliance with us we expected them to continue to grow," said the spokesman.
HHC chief executive officer Stephen Bollenbach struck a deal in December to acquire Bally Entertainment Corp for $3 billion.
"Peter George is on their (HHC's) board and Bollenbach is on ours. We don't see ourselves as a junior partner in this alliance," added the Ladbroke spokesman.
Ladbroke chief executive George became a non-executive director of HHC earlier this month while Bollenbach joined the Ladbroke board.
